c: 'A container is a small virtual machine.'
o: It shares the host's kernel and is isolated by the system; it starts fast but is not a strong wall
It is the same as an image

c: A file is written inside a container, and the container is removed
o: It is gone, unless it was in a volume
It is kept in the image
why: Data you keep goes in a volume.

c: Where is your own code in the size of the image?
o: Tiny: the packages (191 MB) and the model (64 MB) are most of it
why: Measured as folders outside Docker; the real image size was not measured.

c: A settings value that changes between your laptop and a server
o: In the environment, not in the image
why: The same image can then run in any place.

o: A store for images, where FROM and image: pull from
The image is the recipe and files; the container is one running copy
why: Many containers can come from one image.
